live.name: NICKEL HYATT
live.headline: NICKEL HYATT: a threat actor known by many names
live.in_short: NICKEL HYATT is the Secureworks name for an actor also tracked as APT45 and Andariel. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: NICKEL HYATT is the name Secureworks uses for this threat actor.
It is also tracked under other names, including APT45, Andariel, Dark Seoul, Jumpy Pisces, Onyx Sleet, RIFLE Campaign, Silent Chollima, Stonefly and UN614.
The catalogue lists these tools for the actor: ActiveX 0-day, DTrack, HazyLoad, HotCriossant, Rifle, UnitBot and Valefor.
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: NICKEL HYATT
next.headline: NICKEL HYATT (Andariel): North Korea-linked actor that hits South Korean defense and tech targets
next.in_short: NICKEL HYATT, better known as Andariel or APT45, is tracked by several vendors and governments. They tie it to North Korea. It mostly targets South Korean firms with phishing, server flaws and stolen accounts.

sentences.t: The catalogue lists NICKEL HYATT under many names, including APT45, Andariel, Onyx Sleet, Silent Chollima and Stonefly.

CrowdStrike calls its Silent Chollima profile a North Korea-nexus actor active since at least 2007. CrowdStrike assesses it is likely affiliated with Lab 110 within Bureau 3 of the General Reconnaissance Information Bureau.

In 2019 the US Treasury sanctioned Andariel with Lazarus Group and Bluenoroff. Treasury describes Andariel as a Lazarus Group sub-group, designated because of its relationship to North Korea's Reconnaissance General Bureau.
AhnLab's ASEC says Andariel is either in a cooperative relationship with Lazarus or is one of its subsidiary groups. The report does not choose between the two.
Kudelski Security and Sekoia say Andariel used custom ransomware, Maui and H0lyGh0st, for financial theft.

According to ASEC, Andariel usually targets South Korean companies and institutions. Main targets include national defense, political organisations, shipbuilding, energy and telecommunications. Universities, logistics and ICT firms are also hit.
Microsoft describes Onyx Sleet as primarily targeting defense and IT services organisations in South Korea, the United States and India.
Treasury, citing industry and press reporting, says Andariel targets South Korea's government and infrastructure to collect information.

ASEC says Andariel has used spear phishing, watering hole and supply chain attacks. More recently it has exploited the Log4Shell flaw, targeted poorly managed MS-SQL servers and abused legitimate software.
CrowdStrike assesses that Silent Chollima has used Log4Shell.

In 2023 attacks ASEC linked to Andariel, the file-transfer program Innorix Agent was abused to spread malware. ASEC saw signs of spear phishing but could not confirm how the first infection happened. Tools included Go-based backdoors such as Goat RAT and DurianBeacon, and the AndarLoader tool.

ASEC reports that Andariel used RID Hijacking in breaches. The technique alters an account's identifier so a hidden account is treated as an administrator. ASEC says such an account cannot be fully hidden.

South Korea's National Police Agency attributed one case of defense-sector hacking to Andariel. In its account, the group stole login details from a maintenance company employee. In October 2022 it used them to install malware on subcontractor servers. The agency said firms had been breached since late 2022 without knowing it.

Microsoft reports that since early October 2023 Onyx Sleet exploited a JetBrains TeamCity flaw, CVE-2023-42793. It created a new user account, deployed the HazyLoad proxy tool and dumped credentials. Microsoft assesses the activity may be opportunistic.
In November 2023 ASEC assumed Andariel was exploiting an Apache ActiveMQ flaw, CVE-2023-46604, to install NukeSped and TigerRat backdoors. ASEC had no direct logs confirming this link.
Patch internet-facing servers quickly and keep an up-to-date list of the systems you run.
Keep work and personal passwords separate, and review accounts that vendors and maintenance staff use to reach your network.
